response.title: which power station loses the least power when you only use the usb and 12 volt ports
response.answer:
If you're using a portable power station only through USB and 12V DC ports, with the AC inverter turned off, the most efficient models aren't necessarily the ones with the highest capacity or best advertised efficiency.

The important factors are:

Low idle power consumption: How much energy the station uses just by being switched on.

DC conversion efficiency: How much energy is lost converting the battery voltage to USB-C or regulated 12V.

No AC inverter overhead: Keeping the inverter off can eliminate a substantial source of wasted power.

Low-load efficiency: Especially important if you're powering devices drawing only 5–30W.

For example, a station drawing 5W internally wastes 120Wh per day, even before powering anything. That's a significant loss for a 500Wh battery.

Best options for DC-only use
Shop

EcoFlow TRAIL 300 DC

Best for minimal idle loss

288Wh battery, DC-only design. EcoFlow reports just 0.01W no-load consumption, an exceptionally low figure. However, verify whether its available DC connectors suit your 12V devices. 
powerstations.reviews

Shop

Jackery Explorer 300D Portable Power Station

288Wh, DC-only, with USB-C charging up to 140W. Promising for USB-heavy setups, but I haven't found a comparable measured DC idle-power figure.

$209.00 at Jackery

Shop

EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus

1,024Wh with both USB and 12V car-socket output. Independent testing found 91.5% usable energy via USB-C and 87.4% via 12V, although those results aren't low-load idle measurements. 
Best Batteries

My preliminary choice is the EcoFlow TRAIL 300 DC for very low idle consumption, provided its outputs fit your devices. For a conventional 12V cigarette-lighter socket, the DELTA 3 Plus has stronger documented output-efficiency data. There isn't enough standardized testing to declare an absolute winner.

The continuous wattage matters most: a station that's 92% efficient at 100W may be much less efficient at 5W.
